description: Five blocks of logic on two gate inputs each, giving AND, XOR, NAND, NOR, NOT and a flip-flop from every block, with each block able to fold in the result of the block above it

inputs.text: The first gate of the top block, counted as high at 1V and above
The second gate of the top block, counted as high at 1V and above
The first gate of its block, counted as high at 1V and above; with no cable it takes an internal flip-flop clocked by the first gate of the block above, which no jack carries
The second gate of its block, counted as high at 1V and above; with no cable it takes the flip-flop output of the block above, and that empty jack is also what makes this block cascade

outputs.text: 10V while both gates of the top block are at 1V or above
10V while this block's first gate is high and the second thing it compares is high: the AND result of the block above when cascading, or its own second gate when not
10V while exactly one of the top block's two gates is high
10V while exactly one of the two things this block compares is high: its first gate against the XOR of the block above when cascading, or its own two gates when not
10V except while both gates of the top block are at 1V or above, which is the inverse of the AND
The inverse of this block's own AND output, 10V whenever that one is at 0V
10V while both gates of the top block are below 1V
10V while this block's first gate is low and the second thing it compares is low: the NOR of the block above when cascading, or its own second gate when not
10V while the first gate of its block is below 1V; the second gate never reaches this jack
Flips between 0V and 10V on every rise of the top block's second gate past 1V
Flips between 0V and 10V on every rise of whatever its block's second gate carries, which when cascading is the flip-flop output of the block above

notes: a block cascades from the one above it whenever its second gate has no cable; patching that gate makes the block stand on its own, and the first gate has no say in it
an empty gate jack is not silent: a block's first gate falls back to an internal flip-flop clocked by the block above's first gate, and its second gate to that block's FlipFlop output
the module has no controls at all; everything it does is set by which jacks have cables in them
every output is monophonic and is either 0V or 10V
